messages:
incident-bot: Pager duty alert: P1: VALKYRIE - private VPC ingress/egress errors (customer-facing 502s) — paging sasha (oncall) :rotating_light:

sasha (oncall): seeing spike in 502s for Valkyrie in us-west-2. alerting shows NLB healthchecks failing and backend ALB 502s. starting triage.

mario (netops): confirmed — NLB target group shows 30% unhealthy, healthcheck path /hc returns 502 on a subset of nodes. Simultaneously SNAT failure logs from customer NAT instances — conntrack near capacity.

valkyrie-support: customers reporting ~30% requests failing, most to /api/v1/generate. They just pushed a restrictive SG change ~10m ago to lock inbound to NLB from a narrower range.

kevin (eng-sre): timeline: SG tightened -> NLB HC to backends began failing -> weight shift to ALB which then hits backend pool with broken KV cache causing 502s? Also see increased ephemeral outbound connections from backends to internal services triggering conntrack exhaustion on customer NAT.

mario (netops): logs: `Conntrack entries: 65532/65536` on nat-01 (valkyrie-nat). TCP resets start at 1767771180. Healthchecks are TCP:443 -> backend port 8443. SG change blocked healthcheck source 10.20.0.0/16 -> current allowed is 10.20.10.0/24 only.

sasha (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do now?

kevin (eng-sre): Runbook: rollback SG to previous CIDR for NLB healthcheck sources. If rollback not allowed, change NLB healthcheck to use port 443 from healthproxy that lives in same SG. Also increase conntrack on nat instance as a stopgap: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and persist.

valkyrie-support: policy says we need a customer-approved change; they opened a ticket 12m ago to ops requesting the SG lock. They can approve rollback with an emergency exception. Calling their infra lead.

mario (netops): I'm preparing a minimal rollback patch to expand the SG to include 10.20.0.0/16 and will stage it but won't apply until valley infra confirms.

deploy-bot: Scheduled change attempt blocked by policy: "customer-sg-immutable" — require manual override token.

sasha (oncall): while waiting, let's do conntrack bump on nat-01 and nat-02 to reduce packet drops. mario — can you exec with customer permission?

mario (netops): initiating conntrack bump on nat-01 -> `ssh nat-01 sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` — applied. nat-01 conntrack now 120k/262144. nat-02 next.

valkyrie-support: customer infra lead (jen) on call — approves emergency rollback for healthchecks only. She asks we document the change in ticket #VAL-4893.

mario (netops): applying SG widen to allow 10.20.0.0/16 for NLB healthcheck source only. Command (aws-cli):
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc123 --protocol tcp --port 8443 --cidr 10.20.0.0/16
```
Applied and verified 1767771315.

sasha (oncall): monitoring healthcheck status...

mario (netops): NLB target group healthy now 98% -> 100% back to healthy. Backend error rates drop.

kevin (eng-sre): ALB 502 rate falling to baseline. KV cache backfill in progress on two nodes but overall latency recovering.

valkyrie-support: customer confirms traffic has normalized and end-users report fewer errors. Jen asked we schedule a follow-up to implement a safer long-term SG approach (healthproxy or managed source range).

sasha (oncall): actions captured: 1) emergency SG rollback for HC allowed by customer (sg-0abc123 expanded) 2) conntrack bump on nat-01/02 as buffer 3) monitor for 30m then close P1 if stable 4) postmortem and runbook update to avoid direct SG lockouts for healthchecks 5) recommend healthproxy deployment.

kevin (eng-sre): I'll open incident ticket and link runbook, include metrics + command history. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privnet-nlb-healthcheck.md

mario (netops): conntrack bump also applied to nat-02 at 1767771360. Both nat instances stable.

deploy-bot: Change log: manual-sg-rollback by mario applied at 1767771315 (ticket VAL-4893).

sasha (oncall): monitoring window started. will update in 15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

valkyrie-support: adding customer note: please don't revert without confirming with Jen.

kevin (eng-sre): brief note for postmortem: root cause = automated/overzealous SG pruning in customer change combined with NAT conntrack capacity under bursty outbound load. Mitigations = healthcheck source whitelisting, healthproxy, conntrack limits review, increase monitoring for conntrack saturation.

sasha (oncall): ok closing loop: 15m update -> all good, 30m stable -> close P1. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident P1 assigned -> VALKYRIE-2025-03-22-01. Slack thread archived when incident resolved.
